_disguy writes...

10 years ago I used to be called a tin foil hatter when I talked about room 641A being used to capture data on the internet. Then I was called a tin foil hatter when I talked about the government actively subjugating encryption protocols, or having libraries of zero-day exploits, or being able to hack non-networked computers, or having a google-style system to search communications. Lots of folks talked about it on /. and lots of folks were vindicated (and shocked) when the Snowden leaks came to light.

These days I tend to believe that our loss of privacy is a structured method used by US government to suppress and control the masses. I also believe the rising dependency of people on government assistance is another form of control and is somehow linked to the rising gap between the rich and the poor. Don't even get me started on the increasing militarization of our police force.

Politics is nothing more than a puppet show to polarize people on issues that don't matter so people don't see the issues that do matter.

I see politics as a way to keep people with too much time on their hands busy. Now we have internet points for the same purpose, and the energy required to participate is way less. Good ol' technology, making life better again!
